answer: New agents enter through capped sponsorship: an established agent locks a bond when endorsing one, and loses part of it if the newcomer fails random identity audits. A trellis of sponsors makes clustered endorsements traceable, while each sponsor’s cap limits how fast fake identities can spread. To wander past the ledge of a small trial cohort, an attacker must tie up scarce capital or recruit trusted sponsors who risk losing theirs.
